transcript.text: Hi everyone. The public API rate-limit project is up for its production policy review on August 25, and I'll be making the final decision on the policy that gets communicated to customers. Before I record the final policy, I need to hear from each of you on any release-impacting findings from your areas. To recap, the current draft allows 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, applies the same limit to authentication endpoints, and doesn't specify a staffed launch window. I'd like to go around the room — backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations — please share what you've found so we can make sure this policy is solid before it goes out.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Our backend load replay shows the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I haven't updated the policy draft yet because the client test was owned by another team, but this is a critical finding: the current draft's 100 requests per minute would break legitimate bulk-import workflows.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from customer success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that its contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered the clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this is critical: if the policy goes out without accounting for this contractual notice period, we could be in breach with Acme.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. This is critical: the current draft applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which would leave them vulnerable to credential-stuffing attacks. The finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but the 30 requests per minute limit for auth endpoints needs to be reflected in the final policy.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from support operations. We confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I haven't added the coverage block to the launch plan yet because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated. This is critical: the current draft doesn't specify a staffed launch window, and we need to account for this exact availability window when finalizing the policy.
transcript.speaker: A5
